title: Compatibility Score Lifecycle, LTS Branching, and Shim-based Upgrade Tooling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a pragmatic runtime semantic versioning policy centered on a computed Compatibility Score, formalize LTS channel contracts, and deliver a shim-based upgrade tooling strategy to enable seamless minor/patch migrations without breaking customer deployments.
background: We have recurring customer friction during runtime upgrades when minor or 'non-breaking' changes cause client errors due to subtle behavioral or wire-format differences. Existing documents focus on semver and staged rollouts; this ticket creates a lightweight, measurable compatibility contract (Compatibility Score), prescriptive LTS guarantees, and a concrete shim/adapter strategy so consumers can get automatic compatibility fixes at runtime when safe.
proposed_policy: Introduce a Compatibility Score (0-100) attached to every runtime release. Releases with score >= 90 are labeled 'Compat-Guaranteed' for the next minor version window. Breaking-change classification remains explicit (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH) but is augmented by score thresholds and automated shim rules. LTS branches will accept backports only if the change keeps or raises the Compatibility Score above 85. Any change that lowers score below defined thresholds requires a rollout gate and documented migration path.
compatibility_score_definition: The Compatibility Score is computed by the compat-checker CI: weighted aggregation of 1) API contract tests (40%), 2) SDK adapter tests (20%), 3) integration matrix (30%) across supported client versions and common deployment topologies, and 4) behavioral fuzz/regression tests (10%). Score is reported as a deterministic integer. Thresholds: >=90 (green), 75-89 (yellow - guarded rollout), <75 (red - requires manual review/major or deprecation).
breaking_change_classification: Expand the taxonomy: Catastrophic (client crashes/data loss), Behavioral (changes semantics but same surface), Wire-format, Performance-regression, and Optional-feature removal. Each change must list classification and estimated compatibility score delta. Catastrophic or Wire-format changes default to MAJOR unless a shim/adapter guarantees transparency.
deprecation_process: Deprecations must include: reason, sunset date (minimum 90 days after announcement for hosted API; 180 days for Private), automatic shim availability or migration guide, and phasing: Announce -> Warn (logs/headers) -> Shim-only mode -> Removal. Deprecation headers will be added to runtime responses and surfaced in Console per-customer view.
lts_channel_contract: Define two active LTS channels: Stable-LTS (18 month support, security/bug/critical backports only) and Enterprise-LTS (36 month, customer-backed patching with SLA). LTS merges require Compatibility Score >=85 post-backport. LTS branches receive compatibility stamp and explicit changelog entries indicating backport rationale and regression risk.
rollout_gates: Mandatory release gates: unit & compat-check (CI), consumer-canary (5% traffic from diverse customers), integration-canary (internal integration tests + 2 partner customers), metrics-safety (latency/error SLOs), and full-shift. For changes with Compatibility Score 75-89 apply traffic shaping and automatic rollback thresholds. The release system will fail fast if customer error-rate delta > 0.5% or p95 latency increases >15%.
shim_and_adapter_strategy: Ship a binary-level shim layer inside the runtime that translates deprecated/changed wire variants to the current contract. Shims are enabled by default for minor/patch releases labeled 'shim-eligible' and have a telemetry tag. Adapter shims should be small, reversible, and feature-flagged per-customer. Provide an SDK adapter compatibility library for customers who prefer client-side fixes.
upgrade_tooling_spec: Deliver 'compat-upgrade' CLI and a CI job 'compat-checker' that: 1) computes the Compatibility Score, 2) runs compatibility matrix tests across pinned client versions, 3) generates suggested shim rules, and 4) prepares an upgrade playbook with rollback commands. The CLI integrates with Console to create canary cohorts and schedule traffic shifts.
automation_and_tests: Add CI job matrix entries for top-10 most common customer SDK versions and top-3 deployment modes (hosted,dedicated,private). Implement fuzz tests targeting known brittle paths (KV cache, streaming chunk boundaries, function-calling plumbing). Add golden traces to detect semantic regressions in chat/stateful flows.
observability_and_risks: Expose per-release compatibility telemetry: CompatScore, shim-usage-rate, per-customer error deltas, and migration adoption curves. Risks: shim complexity masking deeper regressions, false-positive score inflation, and testing blindspots for custom private deployments. Mitigations include manual review for red/yellow scores and an 'adapter kill-switch' for rapid shim rollback.
acceptance_criteria: compat-checker CI job computes score and reports on PRs
compat-upgrade CLI can generate a shim suggestion for a sample minor change
Release pipeline enforces rollout gates based on Compatibility Score thresholds
LTS branch policy documented and approved by Security and Product
Telemetry surfaces shim-usage and per-customer error deltas in Console
